description: Folding steel-frame chair with a thin padded vinyl seat and back pad, legs open and locked

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Folding steel tube chair, thick padded vinyl seat and a padded rectangular backrest, straight rear tube legs continuing up into the backrest frame, straight front tube legs, a solid side rail joining the front and rear legs on each side, legs open and locked, plastic foot caps Materials: cracked and split red vinyl over thin foam, chipped grey enamel on the steel tubes, surface rust at the pivots and foot caps.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.88. 872/2000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, one canvas. Turntable with --allow-holes: the enclosed background is the gap between seat and back and the space between the legs, real openings.

featureReviews.evidence: Built 0.500 x 0.883 x 0.478 m against the declared 0.45 x 0.88 x 0.55 (proxy 0.48 x 0.88 x 0.54, inside tolerance). Rear tube foot -> knee at 0.57 -> rail at 0.87, front legs crossing to the seat frame at 0.365, seat top 0.41, rungs at 0.167 -- every station the proxy's.
featureReviews.notes: The first build ran the rear frame straight and hung the back pad off it in the air; the proxy END view's knee fixed both.

featureReviews.evidence: Seat 0.40 x 0.045 x 0.36 with a welt, back 0.40 x 0.28 x 0.035 on the upper rear section leaning 26 degrees with it, welts and the scuff patch placed through the pad's own up/normal frame so they sit on its face. Scratch canvas on the vinyl.
featureReviews.notes: The first welt placement had the sign of the lean offset wrong and the welts stood off the pad.

featureReviews.evidence: 22 mm polyline tubes with closed bends, two rungs, four brass ferrules, four rivets at the seat pivots and knees, three rust chips. Frame tone 0x7f8a88 (134) so the back-lit faces stay clear of the gate's band.

name: Folding Padded Banquet Chair
nameTh: เก้าอี้พับบุนวม
notes: The chair set out in rows under a tent for temple fairs, funerals, weddings and school events, which is exactly the repetition a level builder wants. Legs are OPEN and locked; a folded-flat variant would be a different silhouette and is not what this entry describes. The prompt asks for STRAIGHT legs joined by a side rail and deliberately does not name the crossed X folding frame: an X of thin tube drew as three and then four disconnected pieces on two separate plates and was rejected as multiple objects both times, and thin crossed tube is also geometry a low-end prop budget cannot carry. Declared 0.45 x 0.88 x 0.55 m, inside the street-furniture prior of 0.3-1.8 m.
